Subject: Nimbus pilot — quick recap + next steps

Carlos — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- What we heard: Nimbus wants a 6-week pilot focused on inpatient documentation summarization and cost-per-encounter benchmarking; success criteria are (1) 15% reduction in clinician triage time on sampled charts, (2) inference latency <250ms p50, and (3) data-handling confirmation for 180-day audit logs.
- Ask for Nimbus: procurement wants an initial pilot contract + a one-off discount for evaluation and confirmation on retention scope.
- Redwood proposal (high level): Reserved pilot capacity (single dedicated instance) + logging with retention controls; suggested pilot pricing below standard list to expedite procurement.

Next steps I propose:
1) I will send the SOW draft and security questionnaire (attached).
2) Nimbus legal/procurement to confirm required SLA tweaks and the discount band they need to approve internally.
3) Internal: loop in security for a short exception on log-retention and legal for any SOW redlines.

Attachment: Nimbus_Security_Questions_2027.xlsx, Nimbus_SOW_draft_v1.pdf

Thanks — I can be flexible with timing for procurement meetings this week.

Cheers,
Hannah

- Procurement: our internal pilot budget is tight. To greenlight the pilot this quarter we need ~20% off list for the 6-week evaluation and a one-week SLA variance (we can accept standard SLA for production but procurement wants the variance spelled out for the pilot window).
- Security: our InfoSec team flagged two items: (a) confirmation that raw PHI is not stored in persisted tokens and (b) that audit logs can be truncated at 180 days with export capability. We attached a short internal checklist — we'll return the completed questionnaire by EOD tomorrow.

If you can get internal sign-off on discount + the log-retention exception, procurement will put the SOW on the fast track.

-Carlos

Subject: Internal: Nimbus pilot — discount and 180-day retention exception request (need approvals)

Team — forwarding the ask from Nimbus. Short summary:
- Request: 20% pilot discount off the proposed pilot price (NX-3491) and written confirmation that audit logs can be retained for 180 days with export-only access for Nimbus. They also want a one-week SLA variance for the pilot window.
- Why: procurement needs this to route approval this quarter; without the concession they will delay.
- Risk area: retention and export of logs touches our data-handling policy (Dev needs to confirm controls).

What I need from each of you:
- Ben: pricing OK to approve 20% pilot discount for a 6-week pilot? Please confirm if any margin guardrails or revenue recognition caveats I should call out.
- Dev: technical confirmation on 180-day log retention + whether we can provide export-only access to Nimbus while keeping raw PHI protections (high-level answer is fine for procurement). If we require controls/contract language, flag the must-have wording.
- Marcus: ops side — will a one-week SLA variance for the pilot introduce operational risk? If OK, can we commit to a fallback plan?

I've attached the SOW draft and their partially completed questionnaire. I need to respond to Nimbus by EOD tomorrow.

Hannah
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Nimbus pilot — discount and 180-day retention exception request (need approvals)

Hannah / team — quick technical assessment: 

- 180-day audit-log retention: feasible. We currently write structured audit logs to an internal secure bucket; we can implement a retention policy of 180 days scoped to the Nimbus pilot tenant and provide a daily export (S3-compatible) to a customer-managed bucket or provide encrypted archives on request. No raw model weights or persistent KV cache containing PHI will be exposed.
- Export-only access: doable via signed, time-limited export tokens and role-based access. We should require a POA (proof of authority) and an export request workflow so exports are logged and approved internally.
- SLA variance (one week): operationally acceptable provided we add explicit fallback: (1) automatic routing to a compatible lower-cost model variant if latency spikes for >3 consecutive minutes, and (2) a scheduled maintenance blackout communicated 24 hours in advance.

Contract language to include (suggestion):
"Redwood will retain system audit logs for the pilot tenant for a period of 180 days. Customer may request export of audit logs via the agreed export process. Redwood will not persist raw model inputs in retrievable KV stores as part of the pilot deployment."

If legal wants more precision on encryption-at-rest / key custody, I can draft a short appendix.

-Dev
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

Best,
Hannah
